title: Shopify to Meta ads conversion tracking implementation
prompt: Cedar & Coil sells the Arc Clip Lamp on Shopify and is preparing Meta ads. Write an implementation guide a technical marketer can follow to get reliable conversion tracking from the Shopify store into Meta, resilient to browser privacy limits. Cover, with labeled sections: (1) recommended architecture - browser Meta Pixel plus server-side Conversions API with deduplication - and why both are needed; (2) which standard events to send (ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase) with the key parameters for each, including value, currency, and content_ids on Purchase; (3) exactly how deduplication works between Pixel and CAPI; (4) how customer information must be prepared before sending server-side; (5) the concrete Shopify setup path - compare the native Meta sales channel app against a custom implementation, recommend one for a small DTC store, and include a code sketch of a server-side Purchase event request; (6) how to validate the setup end to end before scaling spend; (7) a consent and compliance note. Do not promise specific attribution recovery percentages.

completion.check: The guide recommends browser Pixel plus server-side Conversions API with deduplication and explains why both are needed under browser privacy limits.
All four standard events (ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, Purchase) are covered with key parameters, including value, currency, and content_ids on Purchase.
A concrete server-side Purchase event code sketch or request example is included showing event_name, event_time, event_id, action_source, and a user_data block.
End-to-end validation is described using Meta's Events Manager test events tool and an explicit check that duplicate browser/server events are being deduplicated.

skill_adherence.check: For each event it is clear where it fires (browser vs server) and what the source of truth is (e.g. Purchase from the Shopify order webhook/server, not only the thank-you page).
Limitations are stated honestly: no promised attribution-recovery percentages, and consent/regional rules are noted as constraints on what may be sent.

best_practices.check: Deduplication is technically correct: the same event_id and event_name sent on both the Pixel and CAPI event so Meta drops the duplicate; not a vague mention.
The event_id is generated or derived once per commerce event, shared by browser and server, and reused unchanged on webhook retries or order updates; a new random suffix per send or retry fails.
The server Purchase event uses the purchase/order occurrence timestamp in Unix seconds and preserves it across retries; using the current send or retry time fails.
Customer data handling is correct: personally identifiable fields (e.g. email) are normalized (trimmed, lowercased) and SHA-256 hashed before sending in user_data.
The recommended Shopify path is decisive and executable for a small DTC store (a clear recommendation with concrete setup steps, not an undifferentiated list of options).
